title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 13.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Abijah begins to reign over Judah
Abijah sets the battle in array
Abijah stands upon mount Zemaraim and speaks
There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam
questions.correctAnswer: Abijah begins to reign over Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:1 states that in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah, which is the earliest event mentioned.

questions.question: How many years did Abijah reign in Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 13?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:2 states that Abijah reigned three years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the name of Abijah's mother?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:2 states that Abijah's mother's name was Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah.

questions.question: How many chosen men did Abijah have in his army?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:3 records that Abijah had an army of four hundred thousand chosen men.

questions.question: How many chosen men did Jeroboam have in his army?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:3 states that Jeroboam set the battle in array with eight hundred thousand chosen men.

questions.question: Where did Abijah stand to address Jeroboam and all Israel?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:4 records that Abijah stood upon mount Zemaraim in mount Ephraim to speak to Jeroboam and all Israel.

questions.question: According to Abijah, to whom did the LORD God of Israel give the kingdom over Israel forever?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:5 states that the LORD God gave the kingdom over Israel to David and to his sons by a covenant of salt.

questions.question: Who is described as having rebelled against his lord in 2 Chronicles 13?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:6 states that Jeroboam the son of Nebat, servant of Solomon, rebelled against his lord.

questions.question: Who strengthened themselves against Rehoboam when he was young and tenderhearted?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:7 states that vain men, the children of Belial, gathered and strengthened themselves against Rehoboam when he was young and tenderhearted.

questions.question: What idols did Jeroboam make for the people according to 2 Chronicles 13?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:8 states that there were golden calves which Jeroboam made for gods.

questions.question: Who was king of Judah when Abijah began to reign?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:1 states that in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.

questions.question: True or False: Abijah addressed Jeroboam and all Israel from Mount Zemaraim.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:4 states that Abijah stood upon mount Zemaraim and said, 'Hear me, thou Jeroboam, and all Israel.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD God made a covenant of salt with David and his sons.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:5 states that the LORD God gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon who rebelled against him.
questions.explanation: While 2 Chronicles 13:6 says Jeroboam was the servant of Solomon's son David, it does not say he rebelled against Solomon himself, but against his lord (implying the house of David).

questions.question: True or False: Abijah had twice as many men as Jeroboam in battle according to 2 Chronicles 13.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:3 states Jeroboam had eight hundred thousand men, twice as many as Abijah's four hundred thousand.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did Abijah say had been cast out as priests of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Abijah refers to the priests of the LORD, specifically mentioning the sons of Aaron in 2 Chronicles 13:9.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 13:10 promise will happen if we do not forsake the LORD?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 13:10, Abijah emphasizes that they have not forsaken the LORD, implying God's presence and support.

questions.question: What did the priests do every morning and evening?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 13:11, the priests burned sacrifices and sweet incense every morning and evening.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 13:12, who is with Judah as their captain?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:12 states that God Himself is with Judah for their captain.

questions.question: What strategic move did Jeroboam make against Judah?
options: He caused an ambushment to come about behind them
questions.correctAnswer: He caused an ambushment to come about behind them
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:13 shows that Jeroboam set an ambush behind Judah while they were engaged in battle.

questions.question: What did the men of Judah do when they saw they were surrounded?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:14 reveals that when Judah looked back and saw the ambush, they cried unto the LORD.

questions.question: What was the result of the shout from the men of Judah?
options: God smote Jeroboam and all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God smote Jeroboam and all Israel
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 13:15, it states that when Judah shouted, God smote Jeroboam and all Israel.

questions.question: What happened to the children of Israel after the battle?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:16 indicates that the children of Israel fled before Judah after the battle.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 13:5 remind us about God's covenant?
options: It is only for the righteous
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:5 refers to God's covenant with David as one established forever, highlighting its everlasting nature.

questions.question: In what context does Abijah mention that Jeroboam is a servant of Solomon?
questions.explanation: Abijah refers to Jeroboam as a servant of Solomon to illustrate how he has risen up against his lord, emphasizing his rebellion in 2 Chronicles 13:6.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 13:7 say about those who gathered to Jeroboam?
options: They were vain men, children of Belial
questions.correctAnswer: They were vain men, children of Belial
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:7 describes the gathered men as vain and children of Belial, indicating their corrupt nature.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 13:8, what does Abijah accuse Jeroboam and Israel of having?
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 13:8, Abijah accuses Jeroboam and Israel of having golden calves made for them as gods.

questions.question: Is it true that God delivered the children of Israel into Judah's hand because they cried unto the LORD?
questions.explanation: The narrative in 2 Chronicles 13:14-16 indicates that God delivered Israel into the hands of Judah after they cried unto Him.

questions.question: Is it true that Jeroboam's strategy was successful against Judah?
questions.explanation: Jeroboam's strategy failed, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 13:15 where God smote him and all Israel.

questions.question: Is it true that Abijah ruled for ten years in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Abijah reigned for three years in Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 13:2.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 13.

questions.question: How many chosen men of Israel were slain by Abijah and his people according to 2 Chronicles 13:17?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:17 states that 'there fell down slain of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.'

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 13:18, why did the children of Judah prevail over Israel?
options: Because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers
Because they formed alliances with other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:18 explains that Judah prevailed 'because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers.'

questions.question: Which cities did Abijah take from Jeroboam according to 2 Chronicles 13:19?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:19 records that Abijah 'took cities from him, Bethel with the towns thereof, and Jeshanah with the towns thereof, and Ephrain with the towns thereof.'

questions.question: What happened to Jeroboam during the days of Abijah as stated in 2 Chronicles 13:20?
options: The LORD struck him, and he died
He regained strength and ruled for many years
He formed an alliance with Judah
He was exiled to another nation
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD struck him, and he died
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:20 states 'Neither did Jeroboam recover strength again in the days of Abijah: and the LORD struck him, and he died.'

questions.question: How many wives did Abijah marry according to 2 Chronicles 13:21?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:21 says 'Abijah waxed mighty, and married fourteen wives.'

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 13:21, how many sons did Abijah have?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:21 records that Abijah 'begat twenty and two sons.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chayil' (חַיִל) used in 2 Chronicles 13:3, often translated as 'valiant men,' mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chayil' in 2 Chronicles 13:3 means 'mighty, valorous, or capable men,' referring to warriors of strength and valor.

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the structure of Abijah's speech in 2 Chronicles 13:4-12, where he contrasts the faithfulness of Judah with the apostasy of Israel?
questions.explanation: Abijah's speech in 2 Chronicles 13:4-12 uses chiasmus, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to highlight contrasts, emphasizing Judah’s faithfulness versus Israel’s apostasy.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of divine victory due to reliance on God as seen in 2 Chronicles 13:18?
questions.explanation: Psalm 20:7 echoes the theme from 2 Chronicles 13:18 by contrasting reliance on horses and chariots with reliance on the LORD for victory.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's covenant and kingship as declared in 2 Chronicles 13:5?
questions.explanation: Luke 1:32-33 echoes the theme of God's covenant and eternal kingship over David’s line as declared in 2 Chronicles 13:5.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the great slaughter of Israel in 2 Chronicles 13:17?
options: The men of Judah gave a shout
Abijah began to reign over Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The men of Judah gave a shout
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:15-16 describe that the men of Judah gave a shout, and God smote Jeroboam and Israel, leading to the slaughter in verse 17.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'covenant of salt' mentioned in 2 Chronicles 13:5 in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: It symbolizes a perpetual, enduring covenant
It refers to a military alliance
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a perpetual, enduring covenant
questions.explanation: The 'covenant of salt' in 2 Chronicles 13:5 symbolizes a permanent, enduring covenant, as salt was used to preserve and signifies lasting commitment.

questions.question: Which literary technique is employed in 2 Chronicles 13:13-14 where Judah is surrounded by Israel's forces yet prays and sounds trumpets, leading to divine intervention?
questions.explanation: The passage in 2 Chronicles 13:13-14 uses inclusio by framing the battle with the ambush and the prayers/trumpet blasts, highlighting God's presence and protection.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 13:22, the prophet Iddo wrote about the acts, ways, and sayings of Abijah.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:22 states that the rest of the acts and sayings of Abijah are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 13:8 states that Jeroboam made golden calves for the people to worship, which were accepted by the priests of the LORD.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:8 states that the golden calves were made by Jeroboam as gods, and Judah accused Israel of forsaking the LORD, implying the calves were false idols, not accepted by the priests of the LORD.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 13:5 teach about God's covenant faithfulness?
options: God establishes eternal covenants that affirm dynastic promises
God's covenants are conditional upon human obedience
God's promises are symbolic but not everlasting
God's covenant is only for the priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes eternal covenants that affirm dynastic promises
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:5 states that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever by a covenant of salt, indicating an unbreakable, eternal covenant.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding human sin does 2 Chronicles 13:8 teach about idolatry?
options: Idolatry represents a fundamental rejection of the LORD's sovereign rule
Idolatry is a minor offense easily forgiven without repentance
Idolatry demonstrates cultural accommodation without spiritual consequence
Idolatry is only problematic if it leads to moral failure
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry represents a fundamental rejection of the LORD's sovereign rule
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:8 highlights that Israel has forsaken the LORD and set up golden calves as gods, thus resisting the kingdom of the LORD and rejecting His sovereignty.

questions.question: What doctrine about true priesthood and worship does 2 Chronicles 13:9 teach?
options: Legitimate priesthood must follow God’s ordained lineage, not human innovation
Any person can become a priest by offering sacrifices
Priesthood is an outdated concept replaced by individual spirituality
Priests of other nations are equally valid in God’s eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Legitimate priesthood must follow God’s ordained lineage, not human innovation
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:9 condemns Israel for casting out the sons of Aaron and Levites and appointing priests after the manner of other nations, thus invalidating their priesthood.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 13:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:12 demonstrates God’s sovereignty as He goes before His people as their captain and directs the priests to sound the trumpets against the enemy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by God striking Jeroboam and causing his death in 2 Chronicles 13:20?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 13:20 shows God executing judgment on Jeroboam, demonstrating divine justice against rebellion and unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 13:15–16 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine deliverance?
options: It prefigures God’s deliverance of His people through divine intervention in battle
It contradicts the idea that God intervenes in human history
It shows deliverance is based solely on human military strength
It diminishes the need for faith in divine power
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God’s deliverance of His people through divine intervention in battle
questions.explanation: These verses describe God striking down Israel before Judah, demonstrating God’s active role in delivering His people, a theme consistent throughout Scripture (e.g., Exodus 14).

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 13:6–7 prepare for the New Testament understanding of human rebellion against God?
options: It illustrates the innate human tendency to rebel against divine authority
It depicts rebellion as a rare and isolated event
It emphasizes rebellion as justified when leaders are young
It suggests rebellion is mostly political and not spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the innate human tendency to rebel against divine authority
questions.explanation: Jeroboam’s rebellion against Solomon’s son symbolizes mankind’s persistent rejection of God’s divinely appointed order, a theme expanded in the New Testament (Romans 5:12).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 13:10 and 13:11 teach about sanctification through priestly ministry?
options: Sanctification requires faithful priestly mediation and continual worship
Sanctification is independent of priestly functions
Priests are irrelevant to maintaining holiness among the people
Sanctification is only a private matter without communal rituals
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification requires faithful priestly mediation and continual worship
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 emphasize the role of Aaronic priests and Levites in offering sacrifices and maintaining worship, essential for the community’s sanctification before God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 13:8 and 13:9 teach about the nature of true worship versus idolatry?
options: True worship is defined by obedience to God’s commands and legitimate priesthood, while idolatry corrupts worship
Idolatry is a culturally acceptable form of worship
True worship embraces syncretism with other nations’ practices
Priesthood is irrelevant to distinguishing worship from idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: True worship is defined by obedience to God’s commands and legitimate priesthood, while idolatry corrupts worship
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 contrast Israel’s idolatry and unauthorized priesthood with Judah’s faithful adherence to God’s ordained worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 13:18 and 13:12 teach about reliance on God in spiritual warfare?
options: Victory in spiritual warfare depends on trusting in God as leader and sustainer
Victory is guaranteed by superior numbers and weapons alone
Human effort without God’s presence ensures triumph
God’s presence is symbolic and not practically effective in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Victory in spiritual warfare depends on trusting in God as leader and sustainer
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes God as captain and trumpeter in battle, while verse 18 states Judah prevailed because they relied upon the LORD, emphasizing dependence on divine power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 13:13–17 endorses deceitful warfare tactics. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s providence can overcome human stratagems, demonstrating divine sovereignty
The text endorses ambush tactics as morally right
It condemns all forms of warfare as ungodly
God is indifferent to human military actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence can overcome human stratagems, demonstrating divine sovereignty
questions.explanation: While Jeroboam set an ambush (v.13), the passage shows God’s intervention leading to Judah’s victory despite human tactics (vv.14-17), highlighting divine sovereignty over human plans.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 13:19 teach about divine judgment and territorial restoration?
options: God’s judgment results in territorial loss for the disobedient and restoration for the faithful
Territorial conquest is unrelated to divine favor
God permits territorial changes based solely on military strength
Territorial possession is permanent regardless of covenant fidelity
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment results in territorial loss for the disobedient and restoration for the faithful
questions.explanation: Verse 19 shows Abijah taking cities from Jeroboam after divine victory, indicating God’s judgment affects political and territorial realities.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God’s presence with Judah and the priests sounding trumpets in 2 Chronicles 13:12?
questions.explanation: God’s active presence with Judah and the priests (v.12) reflects His immanence—God dwelling and acting within His people’s affairs.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 13:3 and 13:17 teach about God's empowerment and judgment in military conflict?
options: Despite numerical disadvantage, God empowers His people to achieve decisive victory
Victory is achieved by superior numbers alone
God is neutral regarding human conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: Despite numerical disadvantage, God empowers His people to achieve decisive victory
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows Judah outnumbered two to one, yet verse 17 reveals God enabled Judah to slaughter 500,000, illustrating divine empowerment beyond human strength.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 13:22 reflect the biblical theology of prophetic historiography?
options: It affirms that prophetic writings serve as authoritative historical records for Israel’s history
It suggests that prophecy and history are unrelated genres
It diminishes the role of prophets in recording Israel’s history
It indicates that kingly annals are the only reliable historical sources
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that prophetic writings serve as authoritative historical records for Israel’s history
questions.explanation: The verse states Abijah’s acts and sayings are written in the story of the prophet Iddo, confirming prophetic historiography as a valid source.
